content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole, which I read as follows.

**Left part.** The top-left ring carries CO2H and is linked to a second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C-OH carbon. The next carbon after C-OH bears the NH. So the ring is biphenyl-substituted at C1, OH at C2 and NHN= at C3. The acid sits at the meta position of the first ring, which gives 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone.** NH–N= connects the second ring to C3 of the oxindole.

**Oxindole.** C3 is double-bonded to N, C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The CF3 is on the benzo ring. Numbering the benzo ring from C3a, the carbons run C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. C4 is the carbon next to C3a, and the CF3 is on the carbon one position further, which is C5.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing does not show clear cis/trans geometry for the C=N bond, so I leave it unspecified.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc23)c1O
- Oxindole: C2(=NN...)C(=O)N(Ar)c3ccc(CF3)cc32. Here c3 (C7a) is attached to N, then c c is C7 and C6, then c(CF3) is C5, then c is C4, and c32 is C3a closing onto C3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc23)c1O
